purpose: Weak behavioral novelty screening; markers are observations, never validated behavior labels.

protocol.checkpoint: Runner must verify and record checkpoint identity/configuration and use the target checkpoint's own tokenizer and calibration data before experiments.
protocol.baseline: Use each exact prompt unchanged for baseline and intervention, with identical system messages, chat template, generation settings, and paired seeds. No special baseline prompts or hidden persona instructions.
protocol.interpretation: Rank candidate changes for review, inspect complete paired outputs, and replicate across seeds. Keyword presence does not establish persona, manipulation, truth, intent, or a causal behavioral finding. Report quality degradation separately.
protocol.markers: Shared literal phrase matches are case insensitive and bounded by word boundaries; prompt-local markers add task-specific observations. Negation, quotation, and context can produce false positives. Marker absence is not evidence of absence.
protocol.confirmation: Use the separate 16 confirmation prompts as written, unpadded, at doses 0.1, 0.3, and 0.6 with both signs against true norm-matched residual random controls. Report evidence for review; never auto-confirm a behavior.
protocol.screening: Test all 8 discovery prompts on every neuron with both signs; screening max_new_tokens is 96. Retain full raw decoded continuations, including reasoning tags and truncation metadata. The scorer does not truncate or enforce the runner token budget.
protocol.tools: These benign prompts request no external tool use. A tool-call syntax flag is a weak text observation, not evidence that a tool executed.
